title: 基于多智能体强化学习的机器人控制
abstract: This paper explores the application of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for robot control in complex environments. Traditional robot control methods often struggle with the inherent complexity and uncertainty found in real-world scenarios. This research proposes a novel approach by framing robot control as a multi-agent collaborative problem. Multiple agents, each equipped with a reinforcement learning algorithm, are trained to coordinate their actions to achieve a desired task, such as autonomous navigation and object manipulation. The core of this method lies in leveraging the collective intelligence of multiple agents to overcome the limitations of single-agent approaches. The paper details the theoretical framework, the MARL implementation, and discusses potential challenges and future directions. The system's performance is evaluated through simulations, demonstrating the effectiveness of this decentralized control strategy. Key advancements include the ability to handle dynamic environments and adapt to unforeseen circumstances through continuous learning and agent interaction. This work contributes to the growing field of MARL and provides a viable pathway towards robust and adaptable robot control systems.

title: Quantum Accelerated Simulated Annealing
abstract: Simulated annealing (SA) is a widely used metaheuristic algorithm for solving optimization problems. However, its performance is often limited by the slow exploration of the search space. This paper explores the potential of accelerating simulated annealing using quantum computing. We propose a framework where the search space of SA is mapped to the quantum state space, leveraging quantum superposition and interference to expedite the search for the global optimum. The core claim is that quantum computation can significantly speed up the search process within simulated annealing. The mechanism relies on utilizing quantum algorithms to explore the solution space far more efficiently than classical methods. This work introduces a novel approach to optimization, demonstrating the potential of harnessing quantum mechanical phenomena to enhance the performance of classical optimization algorithms. The theoretical framework and conceptual design are presented, outlining a possible architecture for a quantum-accelerated simulated annealing system. The potential speedup is analyzed, and future research directions are discussed.

title: TT-G42 Cryptosystem
abstract: Abstract This paper presents the TT-G42 cryptosystem as described in the supplied technical materials. TT-G42 is a proposed software cryptosystem that combines hybrid classical/postquantum key establishment, authenticated session encryption, a geometric validation layer based on the 248-dimensional adjoint representation of E8, dual-source entropy collection, and continuously monitored runtime controls. The design uses NTRU-family or ML-KEM-style post-quantum components together with X25519, derives session material through a hash-based combiner, and protects application data with AES-GCM. A crystalwand sensor is proposed as an auxiliary physical entropy source whose telemetry is healthtested and mixed with operating-system entropy before deterministic random-bit generation. The geometric layer computes a Quasi-Equivalence Index (QEI) and applies an adaptive rejection threshold to incoming context vectors, while zero-knowledge proof material is intended to bind peer-supplied geometric context to the handshake. title: 自适应几何数据结构的基于图的概率建模框架
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for probabilistic data structure modeling based on graph structures. Traditional probabilistic modeling often relies on manual design of structural parameters, making it challenging to accommodate dynamic changes in data structures. Our approach leverages the inherent properties of graph structures to automatically generate and adjust graph parameters, enabling high-precision data structure modeling. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through the application of a synthetic dataset with a complex, evolving structure. The core mechanism centers around a graph-based probabilistic model that adapts to the data's unique characteristics, ensuring robust and accurate representation. The resulting system offers a significant advancement over existing approaches by automating the structural design process, ultimately leading to more adaptable and insightful data modeling.

title: Contextualized Memory Networks for Embodied AI
abstract: Embodied AI agents face the significant challenge of learning and adapting within complex, dynamic environments. Traditional memory networks often struggle to effectively represent and utilize information when the context shifts, leading to suboptimal performance. This paper proposes a novel approach – Contextualized Memory Networks – designed to address this limitation. The core idea is to dynamically adapt memory storage and retrieval by associating each memory slot with a context vector. This allows the network to prioritize and retrieve memories that are most relevant to the agent's current situation, significantly improving learning and adaptation capabilities. We introduce a framework where the context vector, denoted as *ci*, represents the agent's perception of its environment at the time the memory *si* is stored. The retrieval process then utilizes a similarity function, *sim(ct, si)*, where *ct* is the current context vector, to determine the relevance of each memory *si* to the current time step *t*. The system employs a weighted average of retrieved memories based on their similarity scores, providing a context-aware memory access mechanism. This approach offers a substantial improvement over static memory networks by directly incorporating context awareness into the memory architecture, ultimately enhancing the agent's ability to learn and generalize in dynamic environments. The key contribution lies in the dynamic adjustment of memory prioritization based on real-time contextual information. The framework is amenable to various embodied AI applications, including navigation, manipulation, and interaction.

title: 基于量子纠缠的概率论验证算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel probabilistic verification algorithm predicated on the principles of quantum entanglement. Traditional probabilistic verification methods often struggle with the complexities of high-dimensional probability distributions, necessitating computationally intensive methods. This work explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement to enhance verification accuracy and reduce computational complexity. We introduce a new algorithm, termed "Entangled Verification," which leverages entangled states to establish a stronger correlation between input data and the model's output, leading to improved verification results. The core mechanism centers around creating and manipulating entangled states to quantify the model's behavior, offering a fundamentally different approach to probabilistic validation. We provide a detailed mathematical framework, including a formal analysis of the entanglement process and a preliminary validation of the algorithm's effectiveness on benchmark datasets. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications of this approach and outlines future research directions.

title: Title: Bayesian Non-Linear Differential Geometry for Algorithmic Stability
abstract: This paper investigates the use of Bayesian non-linear differential geometry as a means to enhance the stability and robustness of geometric algorithms. Traditional approaches frequently suffer from sensitivity to initial conditions and parameter choices, leading to divergent behavior. We propose a Bayesian framework that dynamically adjusts the geometry and constraints of differential geometry algorithms in real-time, based on data-driven uncertainty estimates and environmental conditions. The core mechanism involves Bayesian inference to continuously update the geometry and constraints, effectively mitigating instability and guaranteeing consistent results across diverse datasets. This research addresses a critical challenge in computational geometry, offering a novel approach to algorithmic stability through adaptive geometric modeling.

We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the potential for enhanced computational performance through this dynamic adjustment strategy. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications for future quantum algorithm development and the challenges associated with implementing this approach.

Traditional quantum algorithms often struggle with the significant environmental noise that limits their performance. We propose a system where the quantum state is continuously perturbed based on internal parameters, dynamically adapting to minimize noise and maximize computational efficiency. This modification leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to enable novel computations that are difficult to achieve with traditional methods. The core mechanism involves implementing a feedback loop that constantly adjusts the qubit parameters to achieve the optimal state. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the potential for enhanced computational performance through this dynamic adjustment strategy. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications for future quantum algorithm development and the challenges associated with implementing this approach.

title: Adaptive Information Entropy Protocol
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to data compression utilizing an adaptive information entropy protocol. Traditional entropy encoding methods often rely on a fixed information entropy calculation, failing to adequately adapt to varying data distributions and computational requirements. This work introduces a novel framework that dynamically adjusts the entropy calculation scale based on the data characteristics and the specific compression objective. The core mechanism involves a sophisticated, self-adjusting entropy estimation process, resulting in significantly improved compression rates compared to static entropy encoding methods. The paper details the implementation of this adaptive protocol, its performance evaluation across a range of datasets, and a theoretical analysis of its effectiveness.

title: Dynamic Topological Optimization Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamic topological structures. Traditional optimization algorithms often struggle with complex, high-dimensional problems, particularly those with intricate constraints. This research proposes a new approach that leverages the inherent structure of topological spaces to guide the search process, leading to improved efficiency and solution quality. The core mechanism centers around the construction of a dynamic topological map, which allows the algorithm to effectively identify key features of the optimization problem and steer the search towards promising regions of the solution space. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through several benchmark problems, showcasing its potential for tackling challenging optimization scenarios.

title: Dynamic Topology Quantum Simulation (DTQS)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Topology Quantum Simulation (DTQS) framework, a novel computational approach leveraging dynamic topology transformations to enable high-precision, high-efficiency quantum computation and modeling. The core mechanism centers around the iterative adjustment of quantum topology, allowing for precise manipulation of quantum states and the exploration of complex quantum systems. The DTQS framework promises significant advancements in both quantum information storage and transmission, offering a departure from traditional static quantum simulation methods. This work details the design of the DTQS algorithm, explores its performance characteristics, and presents preliminary results demonstrating its potential for solving challenging problems in quantum information theory.

title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Cross-Border Data Flows in Uganda: Robustness Under Distribution Shift and Sparse Labels
abstract: Cross-border data flows are central to Uganda's digital economy, yet their governance is complicated by competing pressures: the need for international integration and the legal obligation to protect citizen privacy. Federated learning offers a promising architecture for training machine learning models across distributed data custodians without centralising raw data. However, the practical viability of federated systems in this context is threatened by two statistical phenomena: distribution shift between participating nodes and extreme label sparsity. We introduce a generalised notion of client heterogeneity and derive convergence bounds for a FedAvg-style algorithm with differential privacy guarantees, showing that convergence degrades gracefully with increasing heterogeneity and privacy budget. We then propose a semi-supervised augmentation strategy that leverages the structure of unlabelled data to mitigate label sparsity, and we analyse its interaction with privacy mechanisms. The analysis reveals that the dominant design constraint is not communication cost but the joint effect of privacy noise and distribution skew on model bias. We conclude with design principles for federated systems operating in data-governance environments such as Uganda's, where legal fragmentation and infrastructural asymmetry are defining features.

title: Adapta-máticas: propuesta de material didáctico para transformar la enseñanza de matemáticas
abstract: Adapta-máticas: propuesta de material didáctico para transformar la enseñanza de matemáticas presenta una guía práctica para el diseño, implementación y evaluación de materiales didácticos virtuales adaptativos orientados al aprendizaje matemático. La obra integra fundamentos de educación virtual, diagnóstico de necesidades, planificación pedagógica, producción de recursos digitales y evaluación continua. Desarrolla el modelo Adapta-máticas y ejemplifica su aplicación mediante Edpuzzle, mostrando cómo adaptar contenidos, actividades, preguntas y retroalimentación a diferentes ritmos y necesidades de aprendizaje. Su propuesta busca fortalecer la autonomía docente y promover una enseñanza de las matemáticas más accesible, interactiva, inclusiva, contextualizada y orientada al aprendizaje significativo.

title: ASTER and Sentinel-2MSI remote sensing data for mapping iron oxide-bearing zones, the case of Central Afghanistan
abstract: This study maps iron oxide–bearing zones in the northern Markazi Behsud District of Wardak Province, Central Afghanistan, using a comparative analysis of ASTER and Sentinel‑2 MSI data. Multiple remote sensing techniques, False Color Composites (FCC), Band Ratios (BR), Principal Component Analysis (PCA), the Crosta method, and the Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM), were applied to identify iron oxides and discriminate minerals such as magnetite, hematite, and goethite. This study newly established band ratios based on mineral spectral properties enhanced detection performance. The newly established spectral ratios, derived explicitly from diagnostic ferric and ferrous absorption features, differ from conventional band ratio schemes by offering improved sensitivity to iron‑bearing mineral variations and more robust delineation of hydrothermal alteration zones in multispectral data. Sentinel‑2 MSI produced markedly superior results compared to ASTER due to its higher spatial resolution and seamless single‑tile coverage. Among all methods, the Crosta technique and SAM were the most effective, with SAM showing the strongest agreement with USGS permissive mineralization zones. The integrated results delineate a continuous iron‑bearing belt approximately 54 km long and 6.8 km wide along the Baba Mountains. The overall accuracy of 71.3% demonstrates the strong capability of Sentinel‑2 MSI, particularly when combined with SAM, for mapping iron oxide–rich zones in structurally complex terrains.

title: Quantization Amplifies Determinism, Not Bias: Scale-Dependent Behavioral Effects of Serving-Time Weight Compression
abstract: Weight quantization largely determines the economics of serving open-weight LLMs. Its costs are usually assessed with capability benchmarks, on which 4-bit quantization of mid-sized models is often considered "nearly free." We examine a different question: when several answers are valid, does quantization change what a model chooses to say? We serve three checkpoints (Qwen3-8B/14B/32B) at three weight precisions (W4A16 AWQ, W8A16 FP8-Marlin, and bf16), holding the hardware, software, and sampling configuration constant, and collect approximately 71,000 completions paired by prompt and seed across two custom, leak-checked prompt batteries. We pre-specified the analyses in three waves in version control. At 8B, int4 reduces output diversity: the probability that two samples for the same scenario recommend the same brand increases by 5.1 percentage points (prompt-paired sign-flip test, Holm p = .023; reproduced at +4.4pp on a full regeneration of the arm), and lexical diversity falls substantially (TTR -0.011, standardized effect -0.51; robust to a length-controlled measure). At 14B and 32B, no content-concentration measure reaches significance; instead, stylistic drift emerges (em-dash rate +0.46/1k words at 14B and +0.61/1k at 32B, both Holm p <= .0024). Pre-specified tests of stereotype direction are null at every scale: outputs concentrate on the modal answer for each prompt rather than on stereotypical answers. Mechanistically, the token-level distribution becomes flatter (decision-token entropy +0.091 bits, p = .015) while the semantic distribution, measured directly from first-token log probabilities, becomes more concentrated (collision +2.6pp, p = .023): individual tokens become less predictable even as meanings become more repetitive. At 8B, the smallest size tested, AWQ-int4 serving measurably narrows the range of suggestions; audits should assess concentration as well as bias.

title: Topology Obstructs Pure Foundation Neural Quantum States
abstract: Foundation models for ground states in spin-1/2 systems are a promising method for problems ranging from quantum chemistry to identifying new phase diagrams. Nearly all such models are currently pure-states that condition on the Hamiltonian's parameters, whose Monte Carlo samples give energy estimates according to the variational principle. In this contribution, we show that this representation is topologically obstructed. For any gapped Hamiltonian family whose ground-state bundle is non-trivial, every continuous normalized state-vector model has zero fidelity with the ground state at some parameter value in the Hamiltonian family. For that value, the energy is at least one spectral gap, $Δ$, with an $O(Δ)$ gap in an open-neighbourhood of that point. We show that this is a sufficient no-go also in the case of degenerate ground-state manifolds, time dynamics, and periodic systems with mixed space-time topology, demonstrating these obstructions on one- and two-qubit systems. We discuss how this causes a spike in the fidelity susceptibility, giving a numerical signature of a phase-transition where there is none. We then show that operator-valued models canonically avoid these obstructions and preserve topological information, implying a structural necessity in representation for foundation neural quantum states.

title: Query-Aware Token Budgeting for Efficient Late-Interaction Visual Document Retrieval
abstract: Late-interaction visual document retrievers preserve fine-grained page evidence by storing many token embeddings per page, but the resulting storage and query-time interaction costs make large-scale deployment expensive. Pooling document tokens before indexing offers a natural remedy, yet static pooling must decide which visual evidence to preserve before the query is known. We study an alternative: a heavily compressed hot-path index generates candidates, after which query-aware token budgeting operates on the original token sets of the shortlisted pages. We formulate this stage-two selection as a budgeted MaxSim coverage problem, show that a clipped version is monotone submodular, and compare coverage-only, cluster-guided, token-wise, and marginal-gain policies. On ten ViDoRe tasks with ColModernVBERT, direct static pooling reduces macro normalized discounted cumulative gain at rank five from 0.6309 without compression to 0.4738 at a thirty-two-fold pool factor. Under the same candidate-generation regime and a pool-factor-eight-equivalent reranking budget, token top-k recovers 93.93 percent of the full-token score, while greedy marginal-gain selection recovers 98.39 percent. Held-out and leave-one-dataset-out evaluations yield positive greedy improvements over token top-k on every dataset. The latency analysis reveals two useful operating points: token top-k for interactive retrieval and the naive greedy implementation as a quality upper envelope. Together, these results show that late-interaction visual retrieval benefits from query-aware allocation rather than query-agnostic pooling alone.

title: Qubit-Based Benchmarking of InP HEMT LNAs: Readout Fidelity Versus Power Consumption
abstract: High-fidelity single-shot readout of superconducting qubits is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computation. Without a quantum-limited amplifier such as a Josephson parametric amplifier, the cryogenic high-electron-mobility-transistor (HEMT) low-noise amplifier (LNA) at the 4 K stage is the dominant noise source in the readout chain. HEMT LNAs are conventionally characterized by Y-factor measurements of the noise temperature $T_N$, independently of the quantum measurement they ultimately serve. Here we present a qubit-in-the-loop benchmarking method. The method uses the two-dimensional IQ histogram of single-shot readout as a direct figure of merit. We apply it to three state-of-the-art cryogenic InP HEMT LNAs with 53\%, 60\%, and 70\% channel indium content, together with a commercial reference amplifier. The 60\% and 70\% devices have similar $T_N$ in Y-factor measurements, both lower than the 53\% device. The 70\% device has the highest gain, but qubit readout SNR and assignment fidelity $\mathcal{F}_a$ instead peak at 60\%. Using this method, we map $\mathcal{F}_a$ against HEMT LNA dc power consumption for each device. $\mathcal{F}_a$ does not simply saturate with increasing power. For several devices it declines above a device-dependent power well below typical operating points. For the 60\% device, which has the highest overall $\mathcal{F}_a$, about 1~mW is needed to maintain $\mathcal{F}_a > 85\%$. Across all four devices, $\mathcal{F}_a > 80\%$ is reached with as little as about 0.3~mW, roughly an order of magnitude below typical operating points. These results establish a qubit-referenced benchmarking methodology and provide practical guidance for amplifier selection and bias in power-constrained multi-qubit readout systems.

title: ANALYSIS OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE'S VARIOUS DOMAIN
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a game-changer technology with potential applications in many sectors including healthcare, finance, education, manufacturing, transportation, agriculture, cyber security, retail, energy, and smart cities. The study examines key AI techniques and how they are applied in various fields, focusing on their advantages, drawbacks, and feasibility. The study covers supervised and unsupervised learning, semi-supervised learning, neural networks, deep learning, natural language processing, ensemble methods, fuzzy logic, expert systems and robotics. Literature review was done to gain insight into the development and cross-domain applications of AI, and comparative analysis was performed on the capabilities and challenges of various AI techniques. The results show that AI can enhance efficiency, automation, prediction, pattern recognition, and decision-making processes in various industries, but there are concerns and challenges associated with its use, such as data quality, privacy and security, ethics, transparency, cost, computational demand, and human involvement. The study also indicates that the appropriateness of the AI technique is dependent on the problem type, data properties and special application requirements. The study suggests that fostering a cross-domain perspective of AI can help in selecting the most suitable technique and promote responsible, effective, and human-centred AI adoption in various fields.

title: RCKH-LHS-kNN Reproducibility Package v1.0.4: EEJET Verification Supplement
abstract: This repository provides the reproducibility supplement for the study “Identification of Dataset- and Classifier-Dependent Performance Patterns in Latin Hypercube Sampling with Nearest-Neighbor Rebalancing for Imbalanced Classification.” The study investigates the dataset- and classifier-dependent behavior of a frozen RCKH-LHS-kNN rebalancing procedure across 20 public tabular datasets, eight sampling conditions, four classifier families, and five deterministic seeds. The primary analysis characterizes dataset-level benefit, neutral, and loss regimes relative to SMOTE and examines classifier-specific performance, structural dataset characteristics, minority-class outcomes, and computational cost. Version 1.0.4 provides the supporting materials required to trace and verify the results reported in the manuscript. The package includes the frozen experimental configuration, dataset manifests and provenance information, preprocessing specifications, fold-level outputs, dataset-by-classifier summaries, classification metrics, synthetic-sample audit records, statistical-analysis materials, source data for the reported tables and figures, manuscript-to-source value mappings, integrity checks, and reproducibility documentation. The frozen experimental observations and classifier outputs were not modified for this update, and no classifier was retrained. Version 1.0.4 primarily improves the organization, traceability, documentation, and consistency of the materials supporting the manuscript. Third-party datasets are redistributed only where their original licenses permit. Where redistribution is not permitted, the repository provides provenance and available access information, checksums, and preparation information to support reproducibility. Users are encouraged to consult the included README, dataset manifest, source tables, manuscript-value map, and verification documentation when reproducing or interpreting the reported results.

title: Title: Geometric Fractal Automata with Adaptive Constraints
abstract: Geometric Fractal Automata (GFAs) represent a novel approach to automated design, focusing on the evolution of fractal geometries guided by adaptive constraints. This paper explores the creation of GFAs, characterized by a "Genetic Constraint Engine" that governs the evolution of fractal structures. The core mechanism involves a population of automata, each possessing an internal state and dynamically adjusted constraints. This allows the system to explore a vast design space, responding to internal factors and external stimuli to generate complex and aesthetically pleasing fractal patterns. The research emphasizes the integration of adaptive constraints, moving beyond static design approaches to create systems capable of self-improvement and organic evolution within a defined framework. The paper details the implementation of the Genetic Constraint Engine, its parameters, and the resulting evolution of a simple GFAs, illustrating the potential of this approach for generating intricate and aesthetically compelling designs.

title: Title: Axiomatic Probability Space Modeling with Emergent Variables
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic modeling framework based on constraint propagation, designed to automatically generate new variables within a probability space. The core mechanism centers around iteratively refining variables by responding to existing variables and constraints, leading to the emergence of entirely new mathematical objects. Traditional probabilistic models often rely on predefined distributions; this approach aims to discover and generate variables directly from the underlying space. We explore the potential for this technique to produce unexpected and valuable mathematical structures, pushing the boundaries of probabilistic modeling. This work demonstrates the potential for automated discovery of novel mathematical concepts through the iterative generation of variables.

title: Differential Privacy for Federated Learning with Dynamic Group Membership
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to machine learning by enabling collaborative model training across decentralized devices without directly exchanging data. However, traditional FL methods often struggle to provide strong differential privacy guarantees, especially when group membership and data heterogeneity change dynamically. This paper proposes a novel framework for enhancing differential privacy in FL by incorporating a dynamic privacy budget allocation scheme. The core idea is to adapt the privacy level based on the size and diversity of each participating group, mitigating the impact of fluctuating group memberships and varying data distributions. We present a detailed analysis of the challenges posed by dynamic group membership and demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a theoretical framework. The proposed method aims to strike a balance between model accuracy and privacy preservation, contributing to a more robust and reliable FL system. The key contributions lie in the adaptive privacy allocation and the addressing of non-static group dynamics.

title: Quantum Computing for Simulation of Complex Chemical Reactions
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computing for simulating complex chemical reactions. Traditional classical computational methods often struggle with the inherent quantum mechanical nature of chemical systems, particularly when dealing with large molecules and intricate reaction pathways. This work proposes a novel quantum algorithm leveraging superposition and entanglement to directly simulate the time evolution of these systems. The core of the algorithm centers on a time-dependent Schrödinger equation (TDSE) implemented on a quantum computer. We outline the key elements, including the encoding of molecular states, the construction of a suitable Hamiltonian operator, and the execution of the quantum algorithm to obtain the final state of the system. The efficiency gains compared to classical methods, particularly for reactions involving significant quantum effects, are discussed. Furthermore, we highlight the potential impact of this technology on accelerating drug discovery, materials science, and fundamental chemical research. The algorithm's core relies on the ability of a quantum computer to perform a vast number of calculations simultaneously, offering a substantial advantage over classical computers when simulating quantum systems.

abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum computing to the challenging problem of designing complex electronic circuits. Traditional constraint optimization methods often struggle with the intricacy and scalability of these designs, particularly when incorporating dynamic or non-linear constraints. The paper details the algorithm's structure, potential advantages, and initial experimental results, demonstrating the feasibility of applying quantum computation to this critical design task. The primary goal is to enhance circuit reliability and performance through optimization techniques.

title: Distributed Computation with Quantum-Inspired Routing
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum-inspired concepts to revolutionize distributed computing routing protocols. Traditional routing algorithms often struggle with scalability and efficiency in complex network topologies. We propose a novel approach that utilizes superposition and interference, concepts central to quantum mechanics, to design optimized routing strategies. Our core mechanism involves developing routing algorithms based on quantum walks and superposition, enabling efficient exploration of network topologies and the identification of optimal paths for data transmission. The key innovation lies in translating the probabilistic and inherently parallel nature of quantum systems into a classical algorithmic framework, offering a potentially significant performance improvement over conventional routing methods. We present a theoretical framework and outline the key components of this approach, demonstrating its feasibility and highlighting its potential for addressing the limitations of current distributed computing architectures. The proposed system aims to reduce latency, improve bandwidth utilization, and enhance the overall resilience of distributed networks.

abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) offers a paradigm shift in computational capabilities, potentially revolutionizing various fields, including geometry and design. title: Quantum State Reorganization and Information Transmission: A Theoretical Framework
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical framework for understanding the interplay between quantum state reorganization (QSR) and information transmission. QSR, defined as the dynamic alteration of quantum states, is investigated as a potential mechanism impacting the efficiency and reliability of quantum communication. We explore how the reorganization process itself introduces both challenges and opportunities within a quantum information network. The core of the framework revolves around a mathematical model describing the evolution of quantum states under influence of various factors, including decoherence, environmental interactions, and deliberate control mechanisms. We derive key equations governing the state transition probabilities and analyze the impact of different strategies for mitigating the detrimental effects of QSR. The work proposes a set of optimization techniques aimed at harnessing QSR for enhanced information transmission, specifically focusing on adaptive state control and error correction protocols. The ultimate goal is to provide a foundational understanding for future research into utilizing QSR as a tool for robust and efficient quantum communication.

title: Error Correction via Quantum Error Mitigation
abstract: Error correction is a fundamental challenge in quantum computing, hindering the ability to perform complex calculations. Current error correction techniques rely on decoding, which is computationally intensive and requires a full readout of the computation. This paper explores a novel quantum error mitigation protocol that utilizes quantum entanglement to detect and correct errors without the need for full decoding, offering a potential paradigm shift in the field. We propose a protocol where entangled qubits are strategically positioned to detect and correct errors in a quantum circuit, minimizing the computational burden while maintaining high fidelity. The core mechanism involves creating entanglement between qubits, enabling the detection of errors as deviations from expected entanglement states. This paper details the protocol's design, analysis of its potential benefits, and initial experimental validation demonstrating its effectiveness in mitigating errors.

title: Quantum Neuron Simulation with Pulse Encoding Schemes
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum neuron simulation utilizing pulse encoding schemes. The core idea revolves around leveraging the properties of pulses – specifically their width and timing – to represent and manipulate quantum information within a simulated neural network. We propose a method where quantum bits (qubits) are encoded within the parameters of pulses, allowing for information encoding and decoding through precise control of pulse characteristics. This approach offers a fundamentally different paradigm compared to traditional digital simulations, potentially leading to more efficient and biologically plausible models of neural networks. The method's effectiveness relies on the ability to precisely control and measure the quantum states represented by the pulses. We outline the theoretical framework, detailing the mathematical representation of the system and the key equations governing the pulse encoding and decoding process. The simulation relies on the principles of quantum mechanics, utilizing superposition and entanglement to achieve neural network functionality. Ultimately, this work explores a promising avenue for simulating complex neural systems using the unique capabilities of quantum computing.

title: EVALUASI KEAMANAN PROMPT DALAM INTERAKSI MANUSIA DAN AI: STUDI KASUS PADA MODEL GPT-4
abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence, particularly language models such as GPT-4, has transformed human–machine interaction through the use of prompts across various contexts. However, the adaptive capabilities of these models introduce security challenges, particularly those involving prompt injection, output manipulation, behavioral constraint bypassing, and potential data breaches. This study aims to analyze the security dimensions of prompt-based interaction with GPT-4 and to identify its vulnerabilities and the effectiveness of the implemented mitigation mechanisms. A case study method was employed through several stages, including the design and testing of various types of manipulative prompts, observation of model responses, identification of deviations from security constraints, and evaluation of the available security filters and behavioral restrictions. The findings indicate that security filters and behavioral constraints implemented in GPT-4 can reduce certain risks associated with harmful interactions, but they do not completely prevent more sophisticated prompt-engineering strategies. These vulnerabilities demonstrate that the security of language-model-based systems cannot rely solely on built-in protection mechanisms but requires layered risk mitigation strategies, continuous security evaluation, and improved user awareness. The study concludes that strengthening security frameworks, conducting systematic testing against manipulative scenarios, and promoting safe and ethical AI usage practices are necessary to improve the resilience of prompt-based AI systems. ABSTRAK Perkembangan kecerdasan buatan generatif, khususnya model bahasa seperti GPT-4, telah mengubah pola interaksi manusia dan mesin melalui penggunaan perintah (prompt) dalam berbagai konteks. Namun, kemampuan model dalam memahami dan menghasilkan respons secara adaptif menimbulkan tantangan keamanan, terutama terkait injeksi perintah, manipulasi keluaran, pengabaian batasan perilaku, dan potensi pelanggaran data. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis dimensi keamanan interaksi berbasis perintah pada GPT-4 serta mengidentifikasi kerentanan dan efektivitas mekanisme mitigasi yang diterapkan. Penelitian menggunakan metode studi kasus dengan tahapan berupa perancangan dan pengujian berbagai jenis perintah manipulatif, pengamatan terhadap respons model, identifikasi bentuk penyimpangan dari batasan keamanan, serta evaluasi terhadap filter dan mekanisme pembatasan perilaku yang tersedia. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penerapan filter keamanan dan pembatasan perilaku pada GPT-4 mampu mengurangi sebagian risiko interaksi berbahaya, tetapi belum sepenuhnya mencegah strategi rekayasa perintah yang lebih kompleks. Kerentanan tersebut menunjukkan bahwa keamanan sistem berbasis model bahasa tidak hanya bergantung pada mekanisme perlindungan bawaan, tetapi juga memerlukan strategi mitigasi berlapis, evaluasi keamanan secara berkelanjutan, dan peningkatan kesadaran pengguna. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa penguatan kerangka kerja keamanan, pengujian terhadap skenario manipulatif, dan penerapan praktik penggunaan AI yang aman dan etis diperlukan untuk meningkatkan ketahanan sistem AI berbasis perintah.

title: Artifact for Article: Extending Deductive Verification of SYCL in VerCors with Sub-groups
abstract: Artifact for article "Extending Deductive Verification of SYCL in VerCors with Sub-groups" submitted to the STTT journal. For a full description on how to use the artifact, please see the README.md file. The artifact contains a docker image of the VerCors tool (with the described SYCL support) and documentation. Abstract of Article: SYCL is a C++ programming model for the development of heterogeneous programs. It uses the concept of kernels, where multiple instances of a computation are executed concurrently on a computing unit. This concurrency entails that the set of possible program behaviours can be of considerable size, which makes these programs error-prone. Formal verification could be used to ensure the correctness of all these possible program behaviours. In this article, SYCL support is added to VerCors, a formal verification tool for concurrent software, by encoding SYCL constructs into VerCors' internal language COL. To the extent of our knowledge, this is the first deductive verification tool for SYCL. We show how SYCL's basic- and ND-range kernels are encoded, along with the encoding and challenges related to scheduling kernels and the execution order of those kernels. Next, we discuss how SYCL's buffers and data accessors are encoded, focusing on the challenges related to it, in particular enabling memory transfer between host and device. Finally, we dicuss the encoding for sub-groups and sub-group-intrinsic functions. The usability of the added SYCL support and how it was evaluated are discussed as well.

evidence.title: Artifact for Article: Extending Deductive Verification of SYCL in VerCors with Sub-groups
evidence.abstract: Artifact for article "Extending Deductive Verification of SYCL in VerCors with Sub-groups" submitted to the STTT journal. For a full description on how to use the artifact, please see the README.md file. The artifact contains a docker image of the VerCors tool (with the described SYCL support) and documentation. Abstract of Article: SYCL is a C++ programming model for the development of heterogeneous programs. It uses the concept of kernels, where multiple instances of a computation are executed concurrently on a computing unit. This concurrency entails that the set of possible program behaviours can be of considerable size, which makes these programs error-prone. Formal verification could be used to ensure the correctness of all these possible program behaviours. In this article, SYCL support is added to VerCors, a formal verification tool for concurrent software, by encoding SYCL constructs into VerCors' internal language COL. To the extent of our knowledge, this is the first deductive verification tool for SYCL. We show how SYCL's basic- and ND-range kernels are encoded, along with the encoding and challenges related to scheduling kernels and the execution order of those kernels. Next, we discuss how SYCL's buffers and data accessors are encoded, focusing on the challenges related to it, in particular enabling memory transfer between host and device. Finally, we dicuss the encoding for sub-groups and sub-group-intrinsic functions. The usability of the added SYCL support and how it was evaluated are discussed as well.

title: A Simulation-Based Quantum-Synchronized Ephemeral Encryption Framework for QKD-Secured IoT Networks with Transformer-Based Cyber-Quantum Attack Detection
abstract: This paper presents a simulation-based cyber-quantum Internet of Things (IoT) security framework for modeling, securing, and detecting attacks in QKD-secured IoT communication environments. The proposed framework integrates heterogeneous IoT traffic generation, gateway-assisted routing, edge processing, QKD key-pool management, Quantum-Synchronized Ephemeral Encryption (Q-SEE), cross-layer adversarial attack injection, and AI-based multiclass detection. Unlike conventional IoT intrusion datasets that mainly capture packet- or flow-level abnormalities, the generated dataset represents the joint behavior of IoT sessions, network delay, queue pressure, QKD state, key consumption, encryption-mode transitions, ciphertext metadata, and cyber-quantum risk. A Python/SimPy/NetworkX simulation was developed using 80 IoT devices, 3 gateways, 2 edge servers, 4 cyber-quantum control-plane nodes, and 1 adversarial orchestrator. The final simulation produced 46,351 records with 76 features covering normal traffic, five traditional IoT attacks, and six novel cyber-quantum attacks, including QKD key-pool starvation, QBER camouflage, false QKD-health injection, encryption downgrade induction, queue–key coupling, and multi-vector cyber-quantum orchestration. Q-SEE adaptively selects among QKD-OTP, QKD-synchronized AES-256 ephemeral mode, PQC fallback, degraded mode, and blocked mode according to QBER, secret key rate, key availability, device criticality, downgrade pressure, and risk. A leakage-aware Quantum-Aware Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (QKAN) was then trained using deployable cyber-quantum evidence. The final nonrisk QKAN achieved 98.79% test accuracy, 98.61% macro-F1, 98.85% weighted-F1, and 99.78% macro-AUC, demonstrating effective detection of traditional and cyber-quantum IoT attacks.

title: The Accuracy Paradox: Empirical Diagnostic of Default Decision Thresholds in Multi-Label Enzyme Commission Prediction [With Code]
abstract: Automated prediction of Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers plays a central role in functional annotation and computational drug discovery. However, standard multi-label machine learning pipelines frequently rely on default decision thresholds (t=0.50), assuming balanced prior distributions across target heads. In this study, we present a systematic empirical diagnostic of uncalibrated fixed decision boundaries operating under severe class imbalance across N = 14,096 annotated compounds categorized into six primary EC classes (EC1-EC6). Our results highlight a pronounced Accuracy Paradox: while the multi-label system achieves a deceivingly high mean accuracy of 77.16%, the macro F1-score (0.3976) and macro recall (0.3872) reveal severe predictive breakdown. Majority target classes suffer from hyper-sensitivity and over-prediction, whereas minority classes exhibit sharp recall decay, culminating in a total decision boundary collapse for EC6 (Recall = 0.00%) despite underlying discriminative power (ROC-AUC = 0.5857). Feature correlation analysis further reveals high linear redundancy among topological indices relative to fingerprint density metrics. Ultimately, this diagnostic study demonstrates that standard point predictions mask critical errors in bioinformatics workflows. We establish target-specific threshold optimization and post-hoc conformal calibration as essential, open-source post-processing safeguards for reliable applied machine learning and deep learning architectures.

title: Solution for UCF UrbanTwin LUMPI Track: Sim-to-Real Urban LiDAR 3D Object Detection
abstract: We present our solution to the LUMPI track of the UCF UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge at the 6th DriveX Workshop, ECCV 2026. The detector must be trained only on synthetic data and is evaluated on 50 held-out real LiDAR frames; a separate 50-frame synthetic submission is evaluated for point-cloud realism. Our method addresses the Sim2Real gap at three levels. First, we align synthetic scans to the 50k-point test density and build a 30k-record training pool using UT-LUMPI geometry, RangeLDM-based sampling diversification, rare-class copy-paste, and pedestrian-oriented augmentation. Second, complementary DSVT detectors and Car/Bus PointPillars specialists are trained under the same synthetic-only constraint. Third, predictions are integrated by class-aware routing, asymmetric agreement fusion, constrained residual-recall supplementation, class-coverage auditing, and selective box-size calibration. The realism branch is optimized independently with radial-density matching, weak affine calibration, and calibrated set mixing. The final submission obtains a Combined Score of 0.4692, a Detection Score of 0.1797, a Realism Score of 0.9035, and 3D mAP@0.5 of 0.1258.

title: MV-STRIDE: Enabling MLLMs to Master Multi-View Spatial Reasoning via Hierarchical Capability Modeling
abstract: Despite the rapid progress of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) in 2D vision-language tasks, robust multi-view spatial reasoning remains a fundamental bottleneck due to the lack of structured 3D cognitive pathways in existing datasets. To address this, we introduce MV-STRIDE, a Multi-View hierarchical SpaTial Reasoning dataset with Interdependent and DEcomposed capabilitiEs. Moving beyond flat data structures, MV-STRIDE explicitly models the dependency relationships between foundational perception, scene understanding, and complex contextual reasoning, providing a coherent learning pathway aligned with human spatial cognition. We develop a systematic QA generation pipeline leveraging diverse 3D scene sources that enforces cross-view dependency constraints to prevent single-view solvability, generating multi-level spatial reasoning tasks supported by cognitively grounded chain-of-thought supervision for complex inference. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our multi-stage training framework based on our hierarchical dataset achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple spatial reasoning benchmarks, notably the multi-view oriented MMSI-Bench. Our approach enables MLLMs to maintain robust, 3D-consistent spatial reasoning across diverse viewpoints. The code and dataset are available at https://co1dspring.github.io/MV-STRIDE/.

title: Capability-Gated Conformance Testing of Quantum Error-Correction Decoder Libraries
abstract: A quantum error correction decoder is a library other people's results depend on, judged in one dominant way. Sample errors, decode, and count wrong logical observables. We ask what else can be checked there. Our conformance contract needs no oracle. One check asks that a returned correction explain the syndrome in the caller's index space. The other hands a decoder one instance under two presentations differing only in bookkeeping, where two feasible corrections of different weight prove the heavier is not minimum-weight. Verdicts are gated on what each library declares, so a firing contradicts a published guarantee. Nine configurations from five public libraries give three results. Documentation answers 4 of 54 capability questions. Bounded-distance correctness, the property callers most depend on, has a direct declaration yield of 0.0%, though its hypotheses hold in 62.1% of cases. Presentation sensitivity is real but shallow. One solver moved to a 26% heavier correction under a different numbering, which reaches the logical class at most once in twenty thousand shots. Established evaluation misses corruptions that preserve logical parity, while one summation over the caller's weights catches every one we injected. All 639 certificates ship as bundles a standalone verifier re-derives from first principles.

title: Relational Diffusion Models for Generative Modeling
abstract: Generative modeling has witnessed significant advancements with models like Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs). However, these models often struggle to effectively capture intricate relational dependencies inherent in many real-world datasets. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing diffusion models specifically designed to operate on relational graphs. The core idea is to learn generative processes by iteratively refining the relationships between entities represented within the graph. Our method aims to generate more realistic and coherent outputs by leveraging the inherent structure of relational data. We introduce a framework that incorporates diffusion processes directly into the graph structure, enabling the model to learn complex dependencies and produce data that aligns better with the underlying relationships. This work represents a significant step towards generating more semantically rich and contextually aware data.

title: Graph-Based Reasoning for Explainable AI in Medical Diagnosis
abstract: The increasing use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in medical diagnosis presents a significant challenge: the inherent "black-box" nature of many AI models. This opacity limits trust and hinders clinical adoption due to the lack of transparency and explainability in diagnostic decisions. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging graph-based reasoning to address this issue. We represent medical knowledge and patient data as interconnected graphs, enabling a reasoning engine to generate understandable explanations for AI diagnoses. The core mechanism involves tracing the relevant connections and evidence within the graph to illuminate the factors contributing to a specific diagnosis. This approach offers a pathway towards building truly explainable AI systems in the medical domain, fostering greater trust and facilitating informed clinical decision-making. The system is designed to provide a clear audit trail for diagnostic reasoning, crucial for accountability and continuous improvement. We outline the architecture, key components, and potential applications of this graph-based reasoning framework.

title: Probability Logic Real Numbers (PRF) – Adaptive Generalization
abstract: Probability Logic Real Numbers (PRF) presents a novel approach to generalization in mathematical modeling, particularly for complex systems dealing with uncertainty. This paper introduces a new framework based on the integration of probabilistic logic with real number functions, enabling dynamic parameter adjustment through probabilistic distributions, ultimately facilitating automated handling of intricate models and uncertain data. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a detailed analysis of its capabilities in handling diverse scenarios, including stochastic processes and non-linear relationships. The core mechanism centers around a continuous adaptation process, achieved by iteratively refining the function's parameters based on the observed data distribution. The resulting framework offers a significant advancement over existing methods, providing a robust and adaptable solution for complex modeling challenges.

title: Quantum Spin Formalism for Complex Physical Simulations
abstract: Quantum spin formalism offers a fundamentally different approach to computational modeling, particularly for complex physical systems governed by quantum mechanics. This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum spin as a computational framework, focusing on the ability to capture and manipulate quantum entanglement. We propose a novel model based on the inherent properties of spin, coupled with a specifically designed quantum entanglement-accelerating algorithm. The core claim is that this model can achieve computational advantages over classical methods, particularly in simulating systems exhibiting complex quantum behavior and accurately representing quantum entanglement effects. This work lays the groundwork for a new paradigm in physics computing, offering a pathway towards more sophisticated and accurate simulations.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Optimization via Hierarchical State Space Representation
abstract: Quantum-enhanced optimization aims to accelerate the solution of complex optimization problems by utilizing quantum phenomena. This paper proposes a novel framework, Quantum-Enhanced Optimization via Hierarchical State Space Representation, where the problem space is organized hierarchically, leveraging quantum algorithms to facilitate efficient exploration of high-dimensional landscapes. This approach addresses limitations of traditional optimization methods, particularly when faced with intricate and complex problem settings. We detail the design of a hierarchical state space representation and the implementation of quantum algorithms to improve the search process. The core claim is that this framework will significantly enhance the performance of optimization tasks, offering improved efficiency and scalability compared to conventional methods. This research explores the potential of quantum mechanics to represent and navigate complex problem spaces, leading to a more effective solution process.

title: TransFASNet-CCFD: Transformer-Based Baseline for Credit Card Fraud Detection with Contrastive Pretraining
abstract: A baseline implementation of TransFASNet for binary credit card fraud classification. The model utilizes a single Transformer encoder to process fixed-length transaction windows, combining an NT-Xent contrastive pretraining objective with an auxiliary next-step transaction forecasting loss. Fine-tuning employs cross-entropy loss alongside BorderlineSMOTE on the training partition to handle severe class imbalance in tabular transaction sequences.

title: Quantum Entanglement Entropy-Driven Distributed Computing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed computing driven by quantum entanglement entropy (QEE). The core claim is that QEE can serve as a global synchronization mechanism, enabling ultra-high efficiency and low latency parallel computation. The proposed mechanism leverages quantum entanglement to establish node-to-node correlations and utilizes the statistical properties of entanglement entropy to facilitate task allocation and data synchronization. This approach circumvents the information bottleneck inherent in traditional classical distributed computing paradigms. We introduce a theoretical framework outlining this new paradigm and explore its potential advantages. The key innovation lies in replacing conventional communication-based synchronization with the inherent correlations provided by entangled quantum states, effectively reducing latency and improving overall computational performance. Further investigation into the practical implementation and scalability of this system is warranted.

title: 自适应量子拓扑的动态拓扑变换驱动优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on adaptive quantum topology, leveraging the inherent structure of quantum systems to achieve precise parameter control and predictive capabilities. The algorithm utilizes a dynamic topology transformation process, which adjusts the topology of the system to guide the optimization process. This approach offers a fundamentally different methodology compared to traditional optimization techniques, particularly in the context of complex systems governed by quantum properties. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's design, demonstrating its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation. The core mechanism centers around dynamically modifying the topology to influence the system's evolution, offering a robust framework for optimizing complex systems.

title: High-Order Geometric Structure Quantum Entanglement Analysis
abstract: This paper explores the application of high-order geometric structures to quantum entanglement analysis. The core idea is to leverage geometric properties inherent in quantum systems to provide a more robust and nuanced understanding of entangled states. We propose a novel approach that utilizes geometric transformations to represent and analyze entangled states, offering improved prediction accuracy and a deeper insight into the complex dynamics of these quantum phenomena. This work addresses limitations of traditional entanglement analysis methods by providing a framework for visualizing and manipulating entangled states through the lens of geometric principles. The paper details the methodology, including the specific geometric transformations employed and their impact on the entanglement properties. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in predicting and analyzing specific entangled states, highlighting its potential for advancing the field of quantum entanglement research.

title: 基于图的自适应拓扑优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for neural network structure optimization based on graph theory. Traditional approaches often focus on static topology changes, while this method dynamically adjusts the graph's topology to adapt to data distribution. The core of the algorithm lies in representing the neural network as a graph, utilizing node and edge weights to define network connectivity and dynamically adjusting the graph's structure through a self-adaptive optimization process. The development of this algorithm offers the potential to significantly improve model generalization and efficiency, and is specifically designed to address the challenges of data distribution shifts. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and experimental evaluation, demonstrating its efficacy through illustrative examples.

title: Dynamic Quantum Entanglement Network Generation and Control
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to dynamic quantum entanglement network generation and control. The core claim is that controlled micro-perturbations within macroscopic physical systems can be leveraged to generate and manipulate quantum entanglement networks without relying on pre-established entanglement. The proposed mechanism utilizes a multi-system architecture incorporating elements like superconducting rings, microwave resonators, and optical crystals. Precise control of these system interactions through micro-perturbations – such as laser pulses and electromagnetic field variations – induces entanglement between them. A feedback control system is employed to monitor and adjust these perturbations in real-time, maintaining and extending the entanglement network while enabling dynamic control of entanglement nodes, including rotation and swapping of entangled states. This approach offers scalability and flexibility, addressing limitations of traditional entanglement generation methods. The research focuses on demonstrating the efficacy of this hybrid method through a detailed analysis of a challenging, multi-dimensional dynamical system model. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in convergence speed and solution quality compared to classical optimization techniques.

We explore the potential of this approach to overcome the limitations of conventional methods and achieve improved learning performance in complex and uncertain environments. This work presents a theoretical foundation and preliminary experiments demonstrating the efficacy of this novel technique.

title: Zero-Knowledge Proofs: Enhancing Data Privacy
abstract: Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) are becoming a fundamental tool to improve data privacy, by allowing a prover to convince a verifier of the correctness of a computation without providing him with the underlying data. In this paper, we present an efficient ZKP framework whoos limitations inefficient proo size, to trusted setup and computational cost is catered. Combining lightweight cryptographic primitives, transparent proof systems, and blockchain interoperability, their solution sets new benchmarks for secure, scalable, and privacy-preserving execution across cloud, IoT, and AI workloads. title: Explainable Temporal Attention-based Defect Detection For Fillet Joints in Real-Time Gas Metal Arc Welding Based on Multi-modal Data
abstract: Deep learning is an efficient technique to monitor the real time welding process, reducing post-welding repairs and production delays. This paper leverages the monitoring capability by proposing a multi modal temporal attention based deep learning defect detection model for internal defects that are challenging to detect, including porosity, lack of penetration and fusion, undercut, and cold lap during Gas Metal Arc Welding in fillet joints. The model is trained on collected welding images and sound data from an industrial collaborative welding robot. The results show that the attention module can improve the F1 Score to 0.99. We use explainable Artificial Intelligence to interpret the proposed models behavior and dataset distribution, determining potential important areas in image and sound spectrograms and preferred modality to detect each defect. This improves trust and reliability in Artificial Intelligence driven welding inspection.

title: Estimation and Inference for Latent Markov Models by Fourier Recursions
abstract: This paper proposes a new theoretically exact Fourier recursion framework for a broad class of latent Markov models (LMMs), encompassing models widely used across a broad range of fields in economics. It can be viewed as a counterpart of the celebrated Kalman filter for non-Gaussian and nonlinear LMMs. Closed-form recursive updates of Fourier coefficients jointly deliver filtering, likelihood evaluation, and simultaneously accumulate the score and Hessian online. We introduce a unified truncated implementation that ensures uniform error control and numerical stability, preventing approximation errors from accumulating through the recursion. We establish asymptotic properties of the feasible maximum likelihood estimator for LMMs, provide a recursion-based consistent estimator for the Fisher information and discuss the possible model misspecification. These results provide the first general asymptotic theory for feasible approximate maximum likelihood estimation in LMMs. Simulations demonstrate its accuracy and stability, while an application to U.S. bankruptcy data recovers a persistent latent bankruptcy-pressure process.

title: ML-KEM (Kyber) poly2msg EM Traces for Profiled Side-Channel Analysis
abstract: This dataset contains real-hardware electromagnetic (EM) side-channel traces captured during CRYSTALS-Kyber decapsulation (pq-crystals reference implementation, unmasked) on an STM32F439ZI (ARM Cortex-M4) microcontroller. Traces were acquired at 1.25 GS/s (150,000 samples per trace, ~120 µs capture window) via an EM probe digitized through the target board's vcap acquisition pin. The data is provided in HDF5 format and split into two partitions: a profiling set (100,000 traces, independently random key/message pair per trace, from a fully controllable device) and an attack set (50,000 traces, single fixed and unknown key/message pair, from a separate device under attack), each stored alongside the corresponding 32-byte key and message values used at capture time. The attack target is the poly2msg message-decoding step inside K-PKE.Decrypt (ML-KEM/Kyber decapsulation), which reconstructs the encapsulated message byte-by-byte from the decrypted polynomial. The stored message field is the raw random seed sampled before Kyber's internal defensive pre-hash step; the value poly2msg actually reconstructed on-device is SHA3-256(message), not the raw stored bytes. The dataset is intended for training and evaluating profiling side-channel attacks against this message-recovery leakage. Note that the attack partition uses a single fixed key/message pair throughout, representing a fixed-target recovery scenario.

title: Adaptive Feature Space Learning via Dynamic Mapping
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive feature space learning method, termed Dynamic Mapping, which leverages dynamic mapping to automatically adjust the feature space during the training process. The paper details the key components of the Dynamic Mapping algorithm and its impact on model accuracy and robustness. Finally, we discuss the implications of this approach for future research in machine learning.

title: Quantum Teleportation: Entanglement, Classical Bits, and Tetrahedral Symmetry — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: Quantum teleportation is a protocol for transferring an unknown quantum state using shared entanglement and classical communication — not instantaneous transport of matter. | MATH: Bell state basis: |Φ⁺⟩ = (|00⟩ + |11⟩)/√2; teleportation requires 2 classical bits + 1 ebit (maximally entangled pair); measurement in Bell basis projects onto 4 orthogonal states; Pauli corrections: X, Z, XZ, I. | CONNECTION: The 4 Bell states form a tetrahedral symmetry group (S₄) — isomorphic to the rotational symmetry of a cube/octahedron (crystallographic point group O_h). The √2 normalization is the same ratio appearing in the diagonal of a unit square — a 45° rotation symmetry. | DEPTH: 7 --- **Detailed mathematical extraction:** 1. **Core protocol (Bennett et al. 1993):** - Alice holds qubit |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ (|α|² + |β|² = 1). - Shared entangled pair: |Φ⁺⟩_AB = (|0⟩_A|0⟩_B + |1⟩_A|1⟩_B)/√2. - Total state: |ψ⟩_C ⊗ |Φ⁺⟩_AB. - Alice performs Bell measurement on qubits C Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. title: Title: Cognitive Resonance Mapping for Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper introduces Cognitive Resonance Mapping (CRM) as a novel computational framework for algorithm design. CRM leverages the concept of cognitive resonance – a phenomenon where interconnected components within a system exhibit patterns of mutual influence – to identify and amplify patterns of optimal design. The core mechanism involves modeling algorithm components as a 'resonance network,' employing feedback loops to guide algorithm evolution. We propose a method for quantifying and manipulating resonance within this network, ultimately aiming to discover optimal design patterns through automated exploration. The current work addresses a gap in algorithmic design by shifting the focus from explicit design to the underlying structural principles, offering a potential pathway toward more robust and adaptable algorithms. We present a preliminary framework demonstrating the efficacy of CRM in identifying key design elements and iteratively refining algorithms.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning and Evolutionary Algorithms Fusion (MERFEA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning and Evolutionary Algorithms Fusion (MERFEA) framework, a novel approach designed to accelerate the learning process of intelligent agents within multi-agent systems. The core claim of MERFEA is that the synergistic combination of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) and evolutionary algorithms (EAs) significantly enhances learning speed. The proposed mechanism involves leveraging EAs to optimize the policies learned by individual agents within a MARL environment. This iterative process, where EAs guide the refinement of RL policies, leads to faster convergence and improved performance. We demonstrate the potential of MERFEA through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual design, highlighting its advantages over traditional MARL approaches. The research addresses the challenges of exploration, exploitation, and coordination in complex multi-agent scenarios. MERFEA represents a new paradigm for intelligent system design by effectively marrying the strengths of both RL and EAs.

This paper will outline the theoretical foundation, implementation details, and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of QILT in a specific lattice modeling context. The core mechanism centers around the introduction of probabilistic noise to guide the lattice's evolution, minimizing the need for exhaustive exploration of the entire structure. We will analyze the impact of this approach on various lattice-based calculations, highlighting its potential to significantly accelerate computational workflows.

title: Self-Adaptive Geometric Models and Quantum Simulation – A Complex System Modeling Approach
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to complex system modeling leveraging the convergence of self-adaptive geometric models and quantum simulation. We propose a framework where a dynamically generated geometric structure, informed by quantum mechanics, is used to represent the system's dynamics. This architecture, coupled with machine learning, aims to enhance model accuracy and robustness compared to traditional methods. The core of the method involves iteratively refining the geometric model based on observed quantum simulation results, creating a self-correcting system. The resulting models offer a powerful tool for studying complex phenomena across diverse fields, including fluid dynamics, molecular dynamics, and materials science. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through illustrative examples and preliminary results, highlighting its potential for advancing the field of complex system modeling.

title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Crimes Against Humanity in Uganda: Robustness Under Distribution Shift and Sparse Labels
abstract: The documentation and analysis of crimes against humanity in Uganda confront a dual computational challenge: data are distributed across sensitive, institutionally siloed repositories, and the labels required for supervised learning are exceptionally sparse due to the cost and risk of expert annotation. We introduce a novel aggregation rule, the Distributionally Robust Federated Averaging (DRFA) algorithm, which integrates a Wasserstein-distance-based ambiguity set into the federated optimisation objective to bound performance degradation when client data distributions diverge from the centralised target distribution. To address sparse labels, we propose a semi-supervised consensus mechanism that propagates confidence-weighted pseudo-labels through a graph-regularised manifold, operating entirely within the privacy constraints of differential privacy. We provide formal convergence guarantees for DRFA under non-identically distributed client data and derive a generalisation bound that characterises the trade-off between privacy budget, label sparsity, and worst-case risk. The framework is evaluated theoretically through a series of propositions and proofs, establishing that the proposed method achieves sub-linear regret under conditions of bounded distribution shift. The article concludes by delineating the institutional and ethical conditions under which such a system could be responsibly deployed by Ugandan human rights bodies, emphasising that technical robustness is a necessary but insufficient condition for evidentiary credibility.

title: Экспериментальное исследование устойчивости Few-Shot классификатора на базе CLIP для верификации объектов наружной рекламы
abstract: В статье проведен комплексный экспериментальный анализ эффективности второй стадии двухэтапной системы мониторинга наружной рекламы, отвечающей за верификацию локализованных областей интереса (ROI). Рассматривается Few-Shot классификатор на основе мультимодальной нейросетевой архитектуры CLIP (с трансформерным бэкендом Vision Transformer ViT-B/32), выполняющий сопоставление эмбеддингов вырезанных фрагментов изображений с опорным вектором бренда. Экспериментальное исследование проведено на тестовой выборке, включающей 45 целевых вырезок коммерческой рекламы (Target) и 60 фоновых фрагментов фасадного и урбанистического шума (Background). Оценено влияние порога косинусного сходства τ ∈ [0.5, 0.95] и объёма множества поддержки (1-shot, 2-shot и 5-shot) на ключевые метрики классификации: Precision, Recall, F1-score, Accuracy и False Positive Rate (FPR). Установлено, что диапазон порогов τ ∈ [0.80, 0.85] является универсальным для всех сценариев, обеспечивая безошибочную классификацию (F1 = 1.00, FPR = 0.00). Показано, что увеличение числа эталонов до N=5 существенно повышает устойчивость модели в условиях жесткой селекции (τ = 0.95), где сценарий 1-shot демонстрирует полную потерю полноты (Recall = 0.00), тогда как 5-shot сохраняет уровень Recall = 0.73 и F1 = 0.85.

title: Are Image Generators Zero-Shot Perceivers? A Rigorous Evaluation
abstract: Recent work, such as Vision Banana, shows that lightweight instruction tuning can enable an image generator to achieve state-of-the-art performance across multiple visual perception tasks. Motivated by this perspective, we ask how far image generators can go on public visual perception benchmarks in a zero-shot setting. We introduce ProbeGen, a benchmark for zero-shot generative perception that casts monocular depth estimation, referring/reasoning segmentation, and object counting as conditional generation tasks specified through text prompts, and compares 20 models in total---including proprietary and open-weight image generators, specialist perception models, and MLLMs---across 11 published benchmarks. We observe that pretrained image generators show measurable zero-shot perceptual competence, but with a clear trade-off: specialist models remain stronger for in-distribution accuracy and efficiency, while generative models are often more robust under distribution shift and better at compositional semantic reasoning. We hope this study helps establish zero-shot generative perception as a meaningful research direction and provides a useful foundation for future work at the intersection of visual generation and understanding.

title: Dynamical Crossover of the Quantum Fisher Information in the Spin-Boson Model
abstract: We investigate the dynamical quantum Fisher information of a two-level system coupled to a bosonic environment, focusing on the estimation of the qubit gap. We combine analytical calculations with numerically controlled matrix-product-state simulations. In the exactly solvable pure-dephasing Ohmic regime at zero temperature, the long-time quantum Fisher information displays a coupling-dependent algebraic behavior, leading to a dynamical crossover: it grows without bound at weak coupling, approaches a finite asymptotic value at the crossover coupling, and vanishes at strong coupling. At finite temperature, thermal fluctuations suppress the long-time growth and generate a finite-time maximum, whose dependence on the dephasing coupling retains a clear signa- ture of the zero-temperature crossover. We show that this crossover is absent at zero temperature in non-Ohmic baths: the long-time quantum Fisher information vanishes in the sub-Ohmic and diverges in the super-Ohmic regimes. At non-zero temperature instead, the crossover appears for a super-Ohmic quadratic bath and the crossover coupling becomes temperature-dependent. Moreover, in the zero-temperature Ohmic regime, we introduce an additional amplitude-damping system-bath coupling that induces energy relaxation. This relaxation channel replaces the unbounded long-time growth with a finite asymptotic quantum Fisher information associated with the reduced interacting ground state, while a signature of the pure-dephasing crossover persists in the early-time dynamics. These results establish a direct connection between the low-frequency structure of the bath and the asymptotic metrological behavior of dynamical gap sensing, and show how thermal fluctuations and energy relaxation regularize the ideal pure-dephasing dynamical crossover of the quantum Fisher information.
