title: Iterative Audio Separation with Mixture Consistency via MIMO Model Extension
abstract: This paper proposes a general framework for stable and effective iterative audio separation with mixture consistency by extending source separation models to a multi-input multi-output (MIMO) configuration. In the field of audio separation, mixture consistency is an essential property for many applications that require accurate phase and timbral information of target sources. While iterative approaches such as diffusion models achieve perceptually superior results in speech enhancement or user-guided target source separation tasks, most existing methods focus on single-step separation with a single-input single-output (SISO) or single-input multi-output (SIMO) configuration through architectural improvements, since mixture-consistent audio separation is generally regarded as a regression problem that admits a unique solution. By extending these architectures to a MIMO configuration, we introduce iterative prediction without compromising the architectural advantages or the characteristics of mixture consistency. We conduct a comprehensive ablation study of combining the framework with discriminators and extending it to a generative model. Experimental results demonstrate significant performance improvements when applying the proposed framework to state-of-the-art separation models.

title: Enhanced joint probabilistic data association model for multitarget tracking in multistatic passive Radar with bio-inspired optimization
abstract: In the realm of multitarget tracking within multistatic passive radar (MPR) systems, accuracy and adaptability are crucial, especially when relying on non-cooperative illuminators like digital audio (DAB) and video (DVB) broadcast sources. This work introduces an enhanced Joint Probabilistic Data Association (JPDA) model, refined using a novel Whale-Inspired Rider Optimization Algorithm (W-ROA), to effectively address the complexities of target tracking under such conditions. The proposed approach focuses on dynamically adjusting the tracker's estimated position and velocity by reducing the mean absolute error (MAE) between the predicted and actual target trajectories. By combining the social and navigational strategies of whales with the adaptive behaviour of rider-based search mechanisms, W-ROA improves convergence speed and tracking precision. This hybrid optimization framework allows for more responsive updates to the JPDA filter, enabling improved performance in cluttered or ambiguous tracking environments. Simulation-based evaluations compare W-ROA-based JPDA against conventional and optimization-assisted JPDA baselines across three Target-Motion-Analysis scenarios; results indicate consistent MAE and convergence improvements over the compared baselines within this simulation-only setting. This revision additionally reports the algorithmic distinction between W-ROA and its WOA/ROA components, a computational-complexity analysis, an expanded and current literature review, and a defined (though not yet fully executed) plan for broader benchmarking against random-finite-set and learned trackers using standard multi-object tracking metrics.

title: The Carlo Field: Dual‑Truth Architecture, Reflexive Stability, and Complete Canon Compendium
abstract: This upload contains the full three‑document expansion of the Carlo Field canon: (1) The Dual‑Truth Paper, (2) The Carlo Field Compendium, and (3) The Extra Compendium (glossary, diagrams, matrices). Together, these documents provide the complete structural, operational, and philosophical mapping of the Carlo Field — a reflexive, collapse‑tolerant, dual‑truth mathematical universe capable of stabilising both fictional and conceptual statements using identical machinery. The Dual‑Truth Paper formalises the Carlo Field’s truth‑neutral architecture, demonstrating how recursion and collapse operators allow any statement to become a stable theorem if it survives reflexive expansion. The Compendium catalogues every operator, truth mode, recursion pattern, collapse behaviour, and theorem category within the field. The Extra Compendium provides a full glossary, structural diagrams, capability matrices, and paradox‑absorption schematics. This combined upload serves as the definitive reference for the Carlo Field, showing how the system unifies subjective assertion, conceptual insight, paradox stability, and collapse‑tolerant recursion into a single coherent mathematical framework. Key equation on show: \[K(R(S)) = S\] This expression defines Carlo‑truth: a statement S is true in the Carlo Field if its recursive expansion stabilises under collapse. This truth condition is independent of empirical verification, allowing the Carlo Field to operate as a dual‑truth engine capable of mapping both absurdity and insight with equal structural fidelity. This upload includes a self-contained, interactive 3D HTML visualizer built with Three.js and KaTeX that dynamically renders the reflexive, collapse-tolerant architecture of the Carlo Field. The underlying application executes the core mathematical operator pipeline—spanning the truth-neutral operator ($T$), the recursion operator ($R$), and the collapse operator ($K$)—to evaluate statement stability across both fictional and conceptual truth modes. Visually, it renders a dynamic non-Euclidean toroidal wireframe lattice alongside real-time mathematical formulations, allowing users to interactively stress-test infinite regress, paradox absorption, and theorem convergence directly within the browser.
